Court Of Additional Sessions Judge-05,
 South District, Saket Courts : Delhi

sentences.text: 1. An aggrieved lady approached the police with grievance of cruelty against her husband and her in-laws and the police investigated the mater upon registration of FIR and came up with a chargesheet for the offences punishable under Section 498A/406 IPC.
The Magistrate took cognizance and summoned the accused persons.

When the matter came up for consideration on charge, the Ld. Magistrate vide order dated 07.06.2018 opined that charge was made out against the husband under Section- 498A but she discharged the other persons for all offences and also discharged the husband for Section-406 IPC.
The order was challenged and a Ld. ASJ came to the conclusion that the order on charge was not a properly considered order and therefore, he remanded the matter back to the Ld. Magistrate.
The Ld. Magistrate again considered the issue of charge and this time, she passed an order on 16.03.2019.

Vide the said order, the Ld. Magistrate opined that the husband was liable for Section- 498A/406 and one Kanchan Kumari was liable for Section-498A IPC and Dayanand, Kusum, Aarti and Rajeev were liable for Section-323/34 IPC.
This time the husband Sanjeev Kumar and sister-in-law Kanchan Kumari felt aggrieved and challenged the order dated 16.03.2019 by filing revision petitions.
RAKESH 2.
The husband through his revision petition has prayed that KUMAR charge under Section-406 IPC be deleted.
The sister-in-law SINGH Kanchan Kumari through her revision has prayed for setting aside of charge under Section-498A IPC against her.
Both the revision petitions have come to this court by way of general transfer and shall be disposed of by the present common judgment.
3. Both the sides have been heard.
Record perused.
4. The complainant has made allegation to the effect "they are threatening me that they will deny me my gold and jewellery gifted to me by parents and relatives at the time of marriage".
We have to decide if this is sufficient to charge any person for Section-406 IPC or not.

The Ld. Magistrate in her earlier order dated 07.06.2018 had declined to invoke Section- 406 by making following observations:-
"The ingredients of Section-406 of IPC is not attracted in the present case as there was no allegations whatsoever made by the complainant, that the stridhan of the complainant was specifically entrusted to any of the accused persons and that the accused persons had criminally misappropriated the stridhan articles of the complainant and had refused to return them to her despite her requests.
Merely by alleging they will deny the complainant her gold jewellery etc., charges under Section-406 of IPC cannot be framed against any of the accused persons".

5. The same Ld. Magistrate however, while passing the subsequent order dated 16.03.2019 has found Section-406 RAKESH attracted and made following observations:-

sentences.text: KUMAR SINGH "The ingredients of Section-406 of IPC is prima facie shown to 2023.06.01 16:20:31 +0530 be attracted in the present case as the jewellery and the gold are stated to be in possession of the accused as it is alleged that the same is lying in the almirah in Bangalore and in Sangam Vihar, New Delhi.
The complainant has filed a list of the dowry articles, which was handed over to the accused Sanjeev, and the accused Sanjeev has denied having any of the jewellery or gold of the complainant.
The complainant has also filed jewellery bills in support of her said allegations.

Therefore, charge under Section-406 of IPC is made out only against the accused Sanjeev Kumar".
6.

It appears that the Ld. Magistrate while passing the subsequent order assumed a particular fact when she recorded "the accused Sanjeev Kumar has denied having any of the jewellery or gold of the complainant".
It is not clear from where the Ld. Magistrate found such a fact.

In her earlier order,
she had specifically recorded that mere alleging that accused will deny the complainant her jewellery would not attract Section-406 IPC.
It is clear that the term "will" mentioned in the chargesheet in respect of the claim of the complainant was indicating a future uncertain event.
It was this thing which had prevailed over the Ld. Magistrate while passing the earlier order dated 07.06.2018.

However, in subsequent order dated 16.03.2019, the Ld. Magistrate assumed an additional fact which was in present perfect tense indicating that the husband Sanjeev Kumar had denied having any jewellery or gold.
This statement would have some colour of misappropriation.

However, the assumption of Ld. Magistrate was not supported from the record and therefore, RAKESH it seems that the Ld. Magistrate has arrived at wrong conclusion KUMAR SINGH because of her assumption regarding a particular fact.
7.

Ld. Counsel for the complainant has relied upon two judgments i.e. Pratibha Rani vs Suraj Kumar & Ors AIR 1985 SC 628 and Ajay Kr. Ghosh vs Smt. Kajal Ghosh And Anr I (1999) DMC 224 in respect of Section-406 IPC.

sentences.text: Perusal of the judgments however shows that factual position were different.
In the first case, there was specific refusal.
In the second case there was a specific allegation that accused had dishonestly misappropriated the entrusted property.
Clearly, both the cases are distinguishable.
There is no such claim made by the complainant in the chargesheet.
8. It is clear from the aforesaid that Section-406 IPC is not made out against the husband Sanjeev Kumar.

However, if during the course of evidence, any material comes on record which suggests the ingredients of Section-406 IPC, the complainant or the State shall be at liberty to move the Trial Court for addition of charge which may be decided by the Trial Court in accordance with law.

9. So far as the prayer of sister-in-law is concerned, the Ld. Magistrate vide order dated 07.06.2018 had not found any material against the sister-in-law but vide subsequent order dated 16.03.2019,
she found offence under Section-498A to be made out against sister-in-law Kanchan Kumari.

Observations of both the orders are re-produced as under:-
RAKESH KUMAR "There are no specific allegations made against the accused SINGH Kusum Kumari and Kanchan Kumari of having committing any act of cruelty on the complainant falling within the meaning of SINGH 'cruelty' in Secton 498A of Sanjeev Kumar vs ) State (Nct Of Delhi) on 1 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199136786/

sentences.text:
The only specific allegation Date:
2023.06.01 +0530 made against accused Kusum Kumari is regarding incident of 16.05.2013 and in respect of which FIR no. 109/14 is already pending against the said accused.
Further admittedly the accused Sanjeev and the complainant were residing in Bangalore after the marriage and the accused Kusum Kumari and Kanchan Kumari used to visit their house".
"Admittedly, the accused Sanjeev and the complainant were residing in Bangalore after marriage and the accused Kusum Kumari and Kanchan Kumari used to visit their house.
It is alleged that the accused Kanchan Kumari had come to stay with the complainant and the accused Sanjeev in Bangalore and she used to torture the complainant.
The complainant has detailed the incidents of 16.05.2013, where both the accused Sanjeev and Kanchan had brutally beaten the complainant.
The facts alleged by the complainant during the period that she resided in Bangalore prima facie indicates that the accsued Sanjeev and Kanchan used to harass the complainant.

As regards the remaining accused persons namely Kusum, Dayanand, Rajeev and Aarti, they resided in Delhi and there are no specific allegations made against them of having committing any act of cruelty on the complainant falling within the meaning of 'cruelty' in Section-498A of IPC".

10. It appears that the Ld. Magistrate found that the in the present case allegations in respect of Section-498A was detailed vis-a-vis case pending in Bangalore Court and therefore, she opined that it was for the accused persons to take such legal steps as may be required for clubbing of both the cases but in the RAKESH absence of applicability of Section-300 Cr.P.C, the Section-498A KUMAR SINGH IPC was required to be invoked against Kanchan Kumari also.
I am of the view that during the pendency of trials, Section-300 cannot be invoked and further that Cr.P.C does not contemplate stay of proceeding like Section-10 of CPC.
In such circumstances, I agree with the view adopted by the Ld. Magistrate.
Ld. Counsel for revisionist has not been able to point out any law which prohibits continuation of trial at two different places.
The order on charge in respect of Kanchan Kumari is clearly justified.
11. In view of the aforesaid discussion, revision petition no. 203/2019 filed by the Sanjeev Kumar is allowed and charge under Section-406 IPC against him is deleted.

So far as revision petition no.
204/2019 filed by Kanchan Kumari is concerned, the same is dismissed.
12. A copy of this Judgment be sent to the Ld. Trial Court.
13. The revision files be consigned to the Record Room after due compliance.
